dataset.title: CDEM Event Point (OpenData)
dataset.description:
This entity describes Civil Defence Emergence Management (CDEM) Event data which can be used publicly on maps and apps to help inform the public of information relating to Cordon and Evacuation areas.

The CDEM Event Point feature captures the following locations (available from a picklist):

· Safe Forward Point
· Incident Control Point
· Cordon Access Point
· Cordon Road Blocks
· Emergency Operations Centre (EOC)
· Civil Defence Centre (CDC)
· Emergency Coordination Centre (ECC)
· Traffic Management Point (TMP)

There is also a free text field – Event Point Information to allow for general information to be made available about that location e.g. ‘Please report to this Safe Forward Point to be escorted through the cordon’.

It is spatially abstracted to a point.

dataset.title: Flood Extent 50 Year (OpenData)
dataset.description:
This entity describes how far floodwaters could spread during a '1-in-50-year flood'.



A '1-in-50-year flood' means there is a 2% chance of that level of flooding happening in any given year. Similarly, a '1-in-10-year flood' has a 10% chance of occurring in a year.

These probabilities are based on long-term weather and tide records. We also adjust the data to account for future changes in rainfall and sea levels due to climate change.



To estimate flood areas, we use computer models that simulate how stormwater flows through Christchurch’s drainage system. These models test different rainfall durations—from short bursts (30 minutes) to long storms (up to 60 hours). For each flood scenario, the model calculates the deepest flooding expected, the largest of which becomes the final flood extent shown in the data.



This flood extent data is used in a derived model called drvFloodExtent, which combines flood models for all catchments and scenarios and is intersected with Rating Units to generate Property Condition comments on the LIM. Any updates to the flood extent data need to be synced to the derived model to appear on the LIM.



It is spatially abstracted to: Area.

dataset.title: CDEM Road Incident (OpenData)
dataset.description:
This entity describes Civil Defence Emergence Management (CDEM) Incidents which can be used publicly on maps and apps to help inform the public about the locations of roads which are closed or restricted.



The purpose of this entity is to show road closure/restriction information when a line wouldn’t make sense (i.e. some rockfall of a tree across a road might only close the road at that exact location) or to pin point the location of the issue within the road closure.



It can also be used when receiving the initial information about an impacted road, possibly before a crew has been on site to setup a formal closure.



The CDEM Road Closure Incident captures the following point locations (available from a picklist):



· Road Incident Reason – why the road is closed/restricted e.g. Flooding, Rockfall, Crash

· Road Incident impact – how the road is affected by the Closure Reason e.g. Closed, Reduced



Other non-picklist fields:



· Road Incident Start – The date and time the closure/restriction was put in place

· Road Incident End – The date and time the closure/restriction was removed

· Estimated Reopening – The date and time we think the closure/restriction will be removed, based

on the information available at the start time. This can be reviewed and updated as needed.

· Location Description – The name of the road the closure is on e.g. Worcester Street

· Information Description – The detail of the affected location e.g. The road is one lane outside

number 150 Worcester Street. Or: Initial information indicates a tree down at 95 Worcester Street

– information will be updated as soon as more information is known.



It is spatially abstracted to: Point.

dataset.title: Flood Extent 200 Year (OpenData)
dataset.description:
This entity describes how far floodwaters could spread during a '1-in-200-year flood'.



A '1-in-200-year flood' means there is a 0.5% chance of that level of flooding happening in any given year. Similarly, a '1-in-50-year flood' has a 2% chance of occurring in a year.

These probabilities are based on long-term weather and tide records. We also adjust the data to account for future changes in rainfall and sea levels due to climate change.



To estimate flood areas, we use computer models that simulate how stormwater flows through Christchurch’s drainage system. These models test different rainfall durations—from short bursts (30 minutes) to long storms (up to 60 hours). For each flood scenario, the model calculates the deepest flooding expected, the largest of which becomes the final flood extent shown in the data.



This flood extent data is used in a derived model called drvFloodExtent, which combines flood models for all catchments and scenarios and is intersected with Rating Units to generate Property Condition comments on the LIM. Any updates to the flood extent data need to be synced to the derived model to appear on the LIM.



It is spatially abstracted to: Area.

Entity Type: Event.

dataset.title: DP Fixed Floor Level Extent (OpenData)
dataset.description:
This entity describes an area that has been drawn up by a Planning Engineer in the Network Planning Team within Greenspace. The purpose of this shape once intersected with the DPFloodManagement feature class is to derive fixed floor level information which can then be linked to affected properties to dictate the required minimum floor level heights for those properties. The intent is that as changes are made to either this feature class or the DPFloodManagement feature class the view vwdrvDPFixedFloorLevelExtent will rederive the extent accordingly.    It is spatially abstracted to an Area.
      
   Entity Type: Concept.

dataset.title: DP Street Centre Line (OpenData)
dataset.description:
This entity is derived as a copy of the StreetCentreLine feature allowing for the assignment of Road Hierarchies as published in the District Plan. 
   
   These road hierarchies may be different that the road hierarchies set in the StreetCentreLine model as the District Plan only differentiates between the following hierarchies: Collector, Major Arterial, Minor Arterial, Central City Local Distributor, Central City Main Distributor and Local Road. By default, all roads are considered Local Roads, but a Plan Change is required to legally define a road as any other hierarchy. 
   
   This entity can initially be updated using stored procedure CCC.uspUpdatedrvDPStreetCentreLine. This will add new roads, update any of the attributes inherited from the StreetCentreLine feature (e.g. StreetCentreLineID, ServiceStatus and Shape), and delete any features that no longer exist in source table. To this end, this model has an additional Legal Status, two Plan Change identifiers reserved for road changes, as well as a customized trigger to allow updates of SHAPE and ServiceStatus for operative features.
   
   Any changes to road hierarchies are to be updated manually and can follow the normal editing guidelines.
      
   It is spatially abstracted to a Line that is segmented at each intersection (for example Colombo Street is comprised of many segments) and may also be artifically segmented for Uturn bays or to resolve number range discrepancies.
   
   Entity Type: Concept.

      The Feature DPFloodMgmtLakeEllesmereLine contains line geometry

      The area geometry enables the generation of property condition comments.
      
      It is spatially abstracted to an Area.
      
      Entity Type: Concept.

dataset.title: Ww Pipe (OpenData)
dataset.description: WwPipe represents a conduit that performs the primary function of the Wastewater network. The Wastewater network conveys sewage from properties to treatment plants for treatment and disposal. Wastewater is transported through the network either by gravity, by pressure from a pump, or by a vacuum. WwPipe also represents supplementary pipework such as vents or overflows that may not necessarily carry wastewater, but are otherwise connected and part of the network. Wastewater pipes generally service more than one property (e.g. a whole street), in contrast to wastewater laterals which generally only service one property. It is spatially abstracted to a line, and is an edge on the Wastewater network. IDS-compliant WwPipe data will be inserted via the WwPipeStage table. When deleted or edited, the record is Archived. A snapshot of the feature record, before it is edited, will be sent to the archive table immediately prior to the first edit of the day for that record. WwPipe assets are represented in SAP as equipment objects. Entity type: Thing. Projection: New Zealand Transverse Mercator (NZTM) - EPSG: 2193 Vertical datum: New Zealand Vertical Datum 2016 (NZVD2016) - EPSG: 7839

dataset.title: Ww Lateral (OpenData)
dataset.description:
WwLateral represents subsidiary pipework to transport wastewater from buildings and properties to the Wastewater pipe network.



The Wastewater network conveys sewage from properties to treatment plants for treatment and disposal. Wastewater laterals generally only service one property, in contrast to wastewater pipes which generally service more than one property (e.g. a whole street).



It is spatially abstracted to a line and is an edge on the Wastewater network.



IDS-compliant WwLateral data will be inserted via the WwLateralStage table.



When deleted or edited, the record is Archived. A snapshot of the feature record, before it is edited, will be sent to the archive table immediately prior to the first edit of the day for that record.



WwLateral assets are represented in SAP as equipment objects.

Entity type: Thing.

Projection: New Zealand Transverse Mercator (NZTM) - EPSG: 2193
Vertical datum: New Zealand Vertical Datum 2016 (NZVD2016) - EPSG: 7839
